cards.explanation: The answer is that there is no resurrection of the dead. Paul says some in Corinth were saying exactly that, even though it's preached that Christ has been raised (1 Corinthians 15:12). He asks how both can be true. It's like handing someone a warm cookie and telling them cookies don't exist.

The answer is False. Paul says, “If there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised.” (1 Corinthians 15:13). He won't let anybody split the two apart. If nobody rises, then Christ didn't either.

The words are preaching and faith. Paul says, “…our preaching is worthless…” (1 Corinthians 15:14). Everything the apostles proclaimed leans on Christ being raised, and without that, it's a cookie box with nothing inside, friends. Paul goes on, “…and so is your faith.” (1 Corinthians 15:14). The Corinthians' own faith rests on the same thing the apostles' preaching does, so if Christ has not been raised, both go down together.

The answer is false witnesses about God. Paul says they would be “…exposed as false witnesses about God.” (1 Corinthians 15:15). They testified that God raised Christ from the dead. If the dead are not raised, then He didn't raise Him, and their testimony would be false.

The word is futile, and it's Paul's own word. He says, “And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile…” (1 Corinthians 15:17). Faith with nothing underneath it gets you nowhere, like stamping dough that never goes in the oven.

The answer is still in their sins. Paul says, “you are still in your sins.” (1 Corinthians 15:17). If Christ has not been raised, the Corinthians haven't been freed from them. That's the weight Paul puts on the resurrection.

The answer is False. Paul doesn't call it a safe rest. He says that if Christ has not been raised, those who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished (1 Corinthians 15:18). It's one of the heaviest lines in this stretch. Hold on to the next part, friends, because Paul turns it around.

The answer is that they should be pitied more than anyone. Paul says, “If our hope in Christ is for this life alone, we are to be pitied more than all men.” (1 Corinthians 15:19). Notice the condition: it's only if their hope in Christ stops at this life. Paul is showing how much rides on the resurrection.

The answer is that He is the first of many to be raised. Christ is “…the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.” (1 Corinthians 15:20), so more follow Him. Paul says so in verse 23: “then at His coming, those who belong to Him.” (1 Corinthians 15:23). He goes first, and others come after.

The answer is False. Paul says the resurrection of the dead comes also through a man (1 Corinthians 15:21). Death came through a man, and so does the resurrection. No angels are part of that sentence.

The words are Adam and Christ, and Adam is the first man (1 Corinthians 15:45). Paul says, “For as in Adam all die…” (1 Corinthians 15:22). Death came through him, and Paul is about to show who brings life. He finishes the verse with, “…so in Christ all will be made alive.” (1 Corinthians 15:22). Death in one, life in the other, and that's the whole turnaround in one sentence.

The answer is those who belong to Him at His coming. Paul gives the order: “Christ the firstfruits; then at His coming, those who belong to Him.” (1 Corinthians 15:23). He gives the order, not the date. My ovens just stay ready, because no one knows the day or the hour (Matthew 24:36).

The answer is until all His enemies are under His feet. Paul says, “For He must reign until He has put all His enemies under His feet.” (1 Corinthians 15:25). He reigns until the job is done. That's the whole picture, friends.

The answer is death. Paul says, “The last enemy to be destroyed is death.” (1 Corinthians 15:26). Death goes last, and it goes down. Paul says just before this that Christ must reign until He has put all His enemies under His feet (1 Corinthians 15:25).

The answer is True. Paul says, “And when all things have been subjected to Him, then the Son Himself will be made subject to Him who put all things under Him, so that God may be all in all.” (1 Corinthians 15:28). Verse 27 helps here: when it says everything has been put under the Son, this clearly does not include the One who put everything under Him (1 Corinthians 15:27). In other words, the Son is made subject to the Father, and the reason Paul gives is so that God may be all in all.

The answer is True. Paul does ask it: “If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptized for them?” (1 Corinthians 15:29). That's one more question showing how much rides on the resurrection. Paul doesn't say more about it here, so I won't either.
The word is day. Paul says, “I face death every day, brothers…” (1 Corinthians 15:31). Every day, friends, not once in a while. I think that's a heavy thing to carry.

The answer is to live it up since tomorrow we die. That's the saying Paul quotes: “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.” (1 Corinthians 15:32). He brings it up as what would be said if the dead are not raised. That's the condition, friends, and the if is what matters.

The answer is False. Paul warns them not to be deceived, then says, “Bad company corrupts good character.” (1 Corinthians 15:33). So the company they keep does have an effect on their character. That's the warning in his words.

The answer is that some of them are ignorant of God. That's the reason Paul gives: “Sober up as you ought, and stop sinning; for some of you are ignorant of God.” (1 Corinthians 15:34). He says it plainly, friends. That's why the wake-up call is so loud.
